request.spec:
Closing or soft-closing a period now fixes every pool member's cut for that period as it stood at
that moment (the per-period cut cell shows the fixed figure from then on, even when the period
closed after its to-date), and reopening makes it live again.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Closing or soft-closing a period now fixes every pool member's cut for that period as it stood at
that moment (the per-period cut cell shows the fixed figure from then on, even when the period
closed after its to-date), and reopening makes it live again.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The change works: the main `cuts frozen at close` test passes. The other three tests in the spec (scenarios 1–3) still fail, so `bin/e2e` exits 1. I checked that those failures are not caused by this change: I ran the spec once with the freezing turned off, and all three failed at exactly the same steps. That run also failed the main test, as it should without the change. None of the three steps involves pool cuts:

- **Scenario 1, line 194:** the test expects vic's claim dated 2026-03-05 to be refused, but the app accepts it.
- **Scenario 2, line 649:** importing rates shows neither a result nor an error within 8 seconds.
- **Scenario 3, line 1184:** opening the edit form on `c_ben_0` is refused when the test expects it to open.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V115__period_cuts.sql`, adds a `cuts` column to `period`. It holds what the cuts are worked out from at the moment the period closes: the sheet's today, the pot, the people and the pools.
- **Server:**
  - `SheetHistory.cutsNow` takes that record of the sheet as it stands.
  - `PeriodService` saves it on every close, soft-close and automatic close (when the period's grace days run out), and a later close saves it again.
  - Reopening clears it, so the cut is live again.
  - The `/pools/history` endpoint now serves the saved record for any closed or soft-closed period, worked out as of the day it closed. That is why a period closed after its to-date shows the cut as it stood at closing, not at the to-date. A period closed before its to-date now gets a per-period cut cell too.
- **Front end:** no logic changed. The page already works out the per-period cut from whatever the endpoint sends, so I only updated the doc comments in `core/pools.ts` and `features/pools/pools.ts`.

Nothing new is written to the audit file. I can look into the three scenario failures if you want, but they're in other features and outside this change.
